patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: take a cpuset cookie for the interleave node count

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: take a cpuset cookie for the interleave node count

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a memory allocation issue in the Linux kernel's mm/mempolicy module, specifically in the alloc_pages_bulk_interleave function. The problem arises when a concurrent cpuset rebind can cause a torn read of the nodemask_t, leading to an empty mask and incorrect node count. To fix this, the patch takes a cpuset cookie around the count and retries if the mask becomes invalid.

review_comments.author: Huang Ying
review_comments.summary: Identified the issue as a torn read of the nodemask_t due to concurrent cpuset rebinds. Suggested taking a cpuset cookie around the count and retrying if the mask becomes invalid.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v5 00/15] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface

version_history.subject: [PATCH v5 00/15] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 01/15] NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the number of listeners accepted in the listener_set function to prevent a userland request from spinning indefinitely due to excessive nesting loops under sv_lock. The limit is set at 1024, which is considered far above any realistic configuration. The patch introduces a new constant NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX and adds a check in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners() to reject requests with more than this number of listeners. This prevents potential deadlocks and ensures the system remains responsive.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 02/15] NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a validation check for the transport name in the listener_set netlink command before creating a service. The code checks if the provided transport name is one of 'tcp', 'udp', or 'rdma' and rejects any other names. This prevents an arbitrary string from reaching the svc_xprt_create_from_sa function, which can trigger a request_module upcall under nfsd_mutex. The check is done in the nfsd_nl_validate_listeners function before taking the nfsd_mutex lock.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 03/15] SUNRPC: keep the first error in svc_register()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to keep track of the first error encountered during RPC program registration, rather than overwriting it with subsequent errors.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 04/15] SUNRPC: bound the local rpcbind client timeout to 1s
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the timeout for local rpcbind client connections to 1 second. The current default timeouts of 10 seconds for AF_LOCAL and 60 seconds for loopback TCP fallback can cause stalls in NFS server operations, leading to hung-task watchdog warnings. By setting a shorter timeout, the patch reduces the duration of these stalls, but does not eliminate them entirely. A more comprehensive solution would be to make the registration process asynchronous.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 05/15] NFSD: report listener creation failures through extack
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code to report listener creation failures through extack, a mechanism for returning detailed error messages from kernel space to userland. When a listener creation fails, the patch records the attribute and transport name of the failing entry and reports both after the loop. This allows userland to receive more informative error messages when creating listeners, which can help with debugging and troubleshooting.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 06/15] SUNRPC: report local rpcbind calls that get no answer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to report local rpcbind calls that fail without an answer, distinguishing between different types of failures such as transport errors and soft timeouts. It introduces a new counter in the svc_serv structure to track the number of unanswered rpcbind calls, which will be used by later patches to adjust their behavior accordingly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 07/15] SUNRPC: stop svc_register() once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to stop registering programs when rpcbind does not respond. The original implementation would continue trying to register other programs even if one program's call timed out, resulting in unnecessary delays. This change improves performance by breaking out of the loop as soon as a program fails to respond.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 08/15] SUNRPC: stop the svc_unregister() sweep once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_unregister() function to stop sweeping for stale rpcbind entries once it receives no answer from rpcbind. This is done by returning immediately when __svc_unregister() returns -EIO, indicating that rpcbind did not respond. The goal of this change is to reduce the number of timeouts and improve performance in scenarios where a local rpcbind never replies.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 09/15] SUNRPC: stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering. The original behavior caused a local rpcbind timeout for each listener, which could lead to multiple timeouts and failures during teardown. To fix this, the patch introduces a new function `svc_xprt_clear_rpcb_unreg` that clears the `XPT_RPCB_UNREG` flag on remaining transports when rpcbind stops answering. This change improves the robustness of the SUNRPC code by reducing the number of timeouts and potential failures during teardown.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 10/15] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) component of the Linux kernel. When attempting to set up listeners, the code would register each listener individually with rpcbind, which could lead to a high number of timeouts and potentially cause the system to hang. The patch introduces a check for rpcbind failures before creating new listeners, and if a failure is detected, it skips registering with rpcbind for subsequent listeners. This approach reduces the likelihood of timeouts and prevents the system from becoming unresponsive.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 11/15] SUNRPC: check rpc_sockaddr2uaddr() for failure when registering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the SUNRPC code by checking if rpc_sockaddr2uaddr() returns NULL due to memory allocation failure, and returning -ENOMEM instead of proceeding with potentially invalid operations. This ensures that the universal address is properly checked for validity before being used. The fix addresses an issue introduced by a previous commit that removed duplicate universal address generation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 12/15] selftests/nfsd: exercise listener_set request validation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds regression tests for the NFSD_CMD_LISTENER_SET checks in the nfsd_netlink_listener code. The tests cover various invalid listener_set requests, including bad transport names, missing addresses, and malformed entries. The tests use kselftest_harness.h to run in their own network namespace and mount namespace, and they do not create any services or register with rpcbind. The patch also updates the MAINTAINERS file and adds a new directory for nfsd selftests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 13/15] selftests/nfsd: add a per-netns rpcbind stub and the listener round-trips
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-netns rpcbind stub to the selftests/nfsd module, allowing it to serve rpcbind from within each network namespace. The stub is used to register listeners and handle round-trips for various tests, including TCP, UDP, multiple listeners, and IPv6. The patch also includes test cases that cover create, add, and remove paths, as well as LISTENER_GET round trips. By serving rpcbind from within the namespace, the patch resolves issues with listener registration timeouts and ensures proper cleanup of network namespaces.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 14/15] selftests/nfsd: check that listener_set asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to the NFS daemon (nfsd) to ensure that listener_set requests only ask rpcbind once, even if it stops answering. The tests cover various scenarios, including stopping a listener after failure, silent set completion, and bounded version sets. A new function, version_set_only(), is introduced to enable exactly one NFS version in a network namespace. The patch also includes changes to the nfsd_netlink_listener.c file to implement these self-tests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 15/15] selftests/nfsd: check that listener removal asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new test case to the NFS daemon selftest suite. The test checks that when a listener is removed, rpcbind is only asked once to unregister it, rather than once for each listener removed. This ensures that removing multiple listeners does not result in multiple timeouts due to repeated requests to rpcbind.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to harden the netlink listener set interface in the NFS daemon (nfsd) and SUNRPC code. The main goal is to reduce unnecessary timeouts when communicating with rpcbind, which can lead to performance issues. To achieve this, the patches modify the behavior of svc_register(), svc_unregister(), and svc_delete_xprt() functions to stop registering or unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops responding.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton
review_comments.summary: The patches aim to reduce unnecessary timeouts when communicating with rpcbind. The changes are focused on modifying the behavior of svc_register(), svc_unregister(), and svc_delete_xprt() functions to stop registering or unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops responding.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c | 16 +++++++++++-----
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index 5331b89c4281..b6f4d66f612a 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,21 +1995,22 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
+#define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
+
 /**
  * nfsd_nl_validate_listeners - sanity-check the listener list from userland
  * @info: netlink metadata and command arguments
  *
- * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that each entry
- * is well-formed: it parses against the policy, carries both an address and
- * a transport name, and the address is long enough for its family. Doing
- * this up front lets the callers below assume every entry is valid and
- * guarantees we make no changes when the request is malformed.
+ * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that the list is
+ * not oversized and that each entry is well-formed.
  *
  * Return: 0 if every entry is valid, or a negative errno otherwise.
  */
 static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 {
 	const struct nlattr *attr;
+	unsigned int count = 0;
 	int rem;
 
 	nlmsg_for_each_attr_type(attr, NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR, info->nlhdr,
@@ -2018,6 +2019,11 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		struct sockaddr *sa;
 		int err;
 
+		if (++count > NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG(info->extack, "too many listeners");
+			return -E2BIG;
+		}
+
 		err = nla_parse_nested(tb, NFSD_A_SOCK_MAX, attr,
 				       nfsd_sock_nl_policy, info->extack);
 		if (err < 0)

--

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] nfsd: accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder

version_history.subject: [PATCH] nfsd: accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch allows the NFS server to accept and honor backdated timestamps from a client holding an attribute delegation, rather than ignoring them or clamping them to the current time. This change is necessary because clients may intentionally set backdated timestamps during operations like cp -p, rsync -t, or tar -x. The patch updates the nfsd4proc.c file to accept backwards atime and mtime values from a delegation holder, while still enforcing rules for future times and maintaining consistency with RFC 9754.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Chuck Lever questioned whether dp->dl_ctime is the correct value to compare against, noting that it's only sampled once when the delegation is granted and never refreshed; he also pointed out a potential issue where a client can send multiple SETATTRs with TIME_DELEG_MODIFY while holding the delegation, leading to inconsistent ctime updates.
review_comments.raw_body:
^^^^^^^^^^^^

Is dp->dl_ctime the right value to compare against here?  It is sampled
once, when the delegation is granted, and nothing refreshes it after
that:

fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:nfs4_open_delegation() {
    ...
	dp->dl_atime = stat.atime;
	dp->dl_ctime = stat.ctime;
	dp->dl_mtime = stat.mtime;
    ...
}

Is there anything that stops a client from sending more than one SETATTR
with TIME_DELEG_MODIFY while it holds the delegation?

Say the first one carries an mtime T5 that is later than dl_ctime.
nfsd4_vet_deleg_time() returns true, ATTR_CTIME_SET stays set, and the
inode ctime becomes T5.

If a second SETATTR then backdates the mtime to T3, where dl_ctime < T3 <
T5, the comparison is still against the grant-time dl_ctime.  It returns
true again, so ATTR_CTIME_SET stays set and T3 is carried into ia_ctime.

notify_change() -> setattr_copy() -> inode_set_ctime_deleg() then drops
that update, because T3 is older than the T5 already in the inode:

fs/inode.c:inode_set_ctime_deleg() {
    ...
	/* If the update is older than the existing value, skip it. */
	if (timespec64_compare(&update, &cur_ts) <= 0)
		return cur_ts;
    ...
}

The mtime moves back to T3 and the ctime stays at T5, so the ctime is
neither carried from the mtime nor stamped with the current time.  That
looks different from the comment just above it, and from the commit
message: "An mtime that moves backwards sets the ctime to the current
time."

Would comparing against the inode's current ctime work better here?  The
inode is already in hand for the current_time() call at the top of the
function.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged a need to rework the patch to properly handle delegation timestamps, identified another race condition, and plans to push some handling into the VFS layer in v2.
review_comments.raw_body:
Yes, I think we do want to rework it to do that. Additionally, I
noticed another race condition that we ought to fix while we're in
here.

I'll be sending a v2, but I think we have to push some of this handling
into the VFS layer so that it's done under more consistent locking and
properly uses the mgtime infrastructure.

-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
